questions.q: If the domain of the function $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1}}{\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2x - 1}{2}\right)}$~is the interval $( \alpha, \beta ] ,$~then~$\alpha + \beta$& is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given function is& $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1}}{\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2x - 1}{2}\right)}$

For,~$\sin^{- 1}x \text{ and } \cos^{1}x$~to be defined~$- 1 \le x \le 1$~and for~$\sqrt{f\left(x\right)}$~to be defined~$f\left(x\right) \ge 0$~and the denominator of any expression can never be zero.

Thus, to define the domain of the given function, we have~

$- 1 \le \sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1} \le 1, x^{2} - x + 1 \ge 0$~and~$\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2x - 1}{2}\right) > 0$

Taking the common values and using the range of $\sin^{- 1}x$~i.e. for positive values~$0 < \sin^{- 1}x \le \dfrac{π}{2},$~we get

$0 \le x^{2} - x + 1 \le 1$~and~$0 < \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2x - 1}{2}\right) \le \dfrac{π}{2}$

$⇒ x^{2} - x \le 0$~and~$0 < \dfrac{2x - 1}{2} \le 1$

$⇒ x\left(x - 1\right) \le 0$~and~$0 < 2x - 1 \le 2$

$⇒ x \in [ 0, 1 ]$~and~$1 < 2x \le 3$

$⇒ x \in \left[0, 1\right]$~and~\dfrac{1}{2}$< x \le \dfrac{3}{2}$

Now, taking intersection, we get~$x \in \left(\dfrac{1}{2},1\right]$

Given, domain of the function is~ \left(\alpha, \beta\right] = $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2},$1\right]$

$⇒ \alpha = $\dfrac{1}{2}, \beta =$1$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = $\dfrac{3}{2} .

$

We know that the domain of~$\sin^{- 1}x$~is~$- 1 ≤ x ≤ 1$.

$⇒$~From~\left($2\right), x > 0,$~from~ \left($3\right), x \ne \dfrac{1}{3}$

From~\left($4\right), 6 + 2\log_{3}x 0\right)$

$⇒ \log_{3}x < - 3$

$⇒ x < {3}^{- 3}$

$⇒ x < \dfrac{1}{27}$~

From~\left(2\right), \left(3\right), \left($4\right), 0 < x < \dfrac{1}{27} . . . \left(5\right)$

From~\left(1\right), - 1 \le \log_{3x} \left(\dfrac{6 + 2\log_{3}x}{- 5x}\right) \le$1$

$∵ 3x \in \left($0, $\dfrac{1}{9}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{3x} \ge \dfrac{6 + 2\log_{3}x}{- 5x} \ge$3x$

$⇒ - $\dfrac{5}{3} \le$6 + 2\log_{3}x $\le -$15x^{2}$

$⇒ - $\dfrac{23}{6} \le \log_{3}$x $\le \dfrac{- 15x^{2} - 6}{2}

$⇒ {3}^{- $\dfrac{23}{6}} ≤ x ≤ 3$\dfrac{- 15x^{2} - 6}{2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{3\dfrac{23}{6}} \le$x $\le \dfrac{1}{3\dfrac{15x^{2} + 6}{2}}

$⇒ 3$\dfrac{- 23}{6} \le$x < \dfrac{1}{3\dfrac{15x^{2} + 6}{2}} . . . . . . \left(6\right)$, here~$3\dfrac{- 23}{6}$~is very small positive quantity,

From \left(5\right)$~and~\left(6\right), 3\dfrac{- 23}{6} < x < \dfrac{1}{27}, \left[x\right] = 0$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = x$

$⇒$~Range~$g\left(x\right)$~is domain of~$f \left(x\right)$

$⇒ g \left(x\right) \in \l$left(3\dfrac{- 23}{6}, \dfrac{1}{27}\right)$≡ \left(\alpha, \beta\right).

$⇒ {α}^{2} + $\dfrac{5}{β} = \lleft(3\dfrac{- 23}{6}\right)2 + \dfrac{5}{\dfrac{1}{27}} = \lleft(3\dfrac{- 23}{6}\right)$2 + 135 $\approx$135$

Note: This question was bonus in Jee Main April 2023 session.

$Given& $f \left(x + y\right) = 2f \left($x\right)$\cdotf \left(y\right)$~&~$f \left(1\right) = 2$

So f\left($2\right) = {2}^{3}$, Similarly

f\left($3\right) = {2}^{5}, $f\left($4\right) = {2}^{7} . . . . .$

Now

$\mathop{∑}_{k = $1}^{10}f\left(\alpha +$k\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}2f \left(\alpha\right) \cdotf \left(k\right) = $\dfrac{512}{3}\left({2}^{20} -$1\right)$

$⇒ 2f \left(\alpha\right)\mathop{∑}_{k = 1$1}^{10}f\left($k\right) = \dfrac{512}{3}\left({2}^{20} -1\right)$~

$⇒ 2f \left(\alpha\right) \left\{f \left(1\right) + f\left(2\right) ⋯ f\left(10\right)\right\} = $\dfrac{512}{3}\left({2}^{20} -$1\right)$

$⇒ 2f \left(\alpha\right) \left($2 + {2}^{3} + {2}^{5} \ldots\right) = \dfrac{512}{3}\left({2}^{20} -1\right)$

$⇒ $2f \left(\alpha\$right)\dfrac{2 \left( \left({2}^{2}\right)$10 - 1\right)}${{2}^{2} - 1} $=\dfrac{512}{3} \left({2}^{20} -1\right)$

$⇒ 2 \times2f \left(\alpha\right) \times $\dfrac{{2}^{20} - 1}{3} = \dfrac{512}{3}\left({2}^{20} -1\right)$

Now comparing both side we get

4f\left(\alpha\right) =$512 ⇒ $f\left(\alpha\right) =$128$

$⇒ $f\left(\alpha\right) = {2}^{7}$⇒ $\alpha =$4$.

questions.q: If the functions are defined as $f ( x ) = \sqrt{x}$ and $g ( x ) = \sqrt{1 - x},$~then what is the common domain of the following functions: $f + g, f - g, f / g, g / f, g - f$, where \left(f \pm g\right)\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) \pm g\left(x\right), \left(f / g\right)\left(x\right) = \dfrac{f ( x )}{g ( x )}
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f ( x ) + g ( x ) = \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{1 - x},$~domain~ \left[0, 1\right]$

$f ( x ) - g ( x ) = \sqrt{x} - \sqrt{1 - x},$~domain~ \left[0, 1\right]$

$g ( x ) - f ( x ) = \sqrt{1 - x} - \sqrt{x},$~domain~ \left[0, 1\right]$

$\dfrac{f ( x )}{g ( x )} = \dfrac{x}{1 - x},$~domain~$[ 0, 1 )$

$\dfrac{g ( x )}{f ( x )} = \dfrac{1 - x}{x},$~domain~$( 0, 1 ]$

So, common domain is \left(0, 1\right)$

questions.q: If& $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left(tan{1}^{°}\right)x + \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(123\right)}{x\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(1234\right) - \left(tan{1}^{°}\right)}, x > 0$, then the~least value of~$f\left(f \left(x\right)\right) + f \left(f \left(\dfrac{4}{x}\right)\right) \text{ and } is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left(tan{1}^{°}\right)x + \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(123\right)}{x\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(1234\right) - \left(tan{1}^{°}\right)}, x > 0$

Now, let~$tan{1}^{°} = a, \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(123\right) = b$~and~$\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(1234\right) = c$

So,~$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{ax + b}{cx - a}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{af\left(x\right) + b}{cf\left(x\right) - a}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{a\left(\dfrac{ax + b}{cx - a}\right) + b}{c\left(\dfrac{ax + b}{cx - a}\right) - a}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{a^{2}x + ab + b\left(cx - a\right)}{acx + bc - a\left(cx - a\right)} = \dfrac{a^{2}x + bcx}{bc + a^{2}} = x$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) + f\left(f\left(\dfrac{4}{x}\right)\right) = x + \dfrac{4}{x}$

$∵ x > 0$,~then least value~$= \sqrt{x \cdot \dfrac{4}{x}} = 2$

Now we get the common region here as

From~ \left(2\right)$~we get that
$⇒ - 1 \le $\dfrac{2x^{2} - 3x + 4}{3x - 5} \le$1$

and~$\dfrac{2x^{2} - 3x + 4}{3x - 5} \le1 . . . . . \left($4\right)$

From~ \left($3\right)$~we get
$⇒ $\dfrac{2x^{2} - 3x + 4}{3x - 5} +$1 ≥ 0$

$⇒ x \in $\$left[\dfrac{- 1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right]∪ \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \infty\right) . . . . .\left(b\right)$

From~ \left($4\right)$~we get
$⇒ $\dfrac{2x^{2} - 3x + 4}{3x - 5} -$1 ≤ 0$

$⇒ $\dfrac{2x^{2} - 6x + 9}{3x - 5} \le$0$

As~$D = \left(-$6\right)2 - $4\left($2\$right)\left($9\right) 0$, we observe that~$2x^{2} - 6x + 9 > 0 ∀ x \in $\mathbb{R}
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3x - 5} \le0 \left($∵ 2x^{2} - 6x + 9 > 0 ∀ x \in R\right)$

$⇒ x \in \left(- \infty , $\dfrac{5}{3}\right) . . . . . . \left($c\right)$

$⇒$ Intersection of $( a ) , ( b )$ and $( c )$~gives us
$x \in \left(- \dfrac{1}{2}, - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)∪ \$left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right).

On comparing this with~\left(\alpha, \beta\right)∪ \left(\gamma, \delta\right),
$⇒ {α}^{2} + {β}^{2} + {γ}^{2} + {δ}^{2} = \dfrac{10}{9}$

questions.q: $Let& $f  \left(x\right)$~and~$g  \left(x\right)$~be two real polynomials of degree~$2$~and~$1$~respectively. If~f\$lleft(g\left($x\right)\right) = 8x^{2} - 2x$, and~$g  \left($f \left($x\right)\right) = 4x^{2} + 6x + 1$,~then the value of~f\left($2\right) + $g\left($2\right)& is ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $f \left(g \left($x\right) = 8x^{2} - 2x\right$and $g \left($f \left($x\right) = 4x^{2} + 6x + 1\right$

Let~f\left($x\right) = cx^{2} + dx + e$~and~g\left($x\right) = ax + b$

So,~f\lleft(g\left(x\right)\right) = c\left(ax + b\right)2 + d\left(ax + b\right) + e = 8x^{2} - 2x$

and~g\l$left(f\left($x\right)\right) = $a\left($cx^{2} + dx + e\right) + b = 4x^{2} + 6x + 1$

On comparing both side we get,~$a = 2, b = - 1, c = 2, d = 3, e = 1$

So,~g\left($x\right) = 2x - 1 ⇒ $g\left($2\right) = 3$

$& $f\left($x\right) = 2x^{2} + 3x + 1$

f\left($2\right) = 8 + 6 + 1 = 15$.

So,~f\left($2\right) + $g\left($2\right) = 18$

$

questions.q: If $S=\{a \in \mathbf{R}:|2 a-1|=3[a]+2\{a\}\}$, where $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$ and $\{t\}$ represents the fractional part of $t$, then $72 \sum_{a \in S} a$ is equal to ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |2 \mathrm{a}-1|=3[\mathrm{a}]+2\{\mathrm{a}\} \\ & |2 \mathrm{a}-1|=[\mathrm{a}]+2 \mathrm{a}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Case-1 }: \mathrm{a} \gt \frac{1}{2} \\ & 2 a-1=[a]+2 a \\ & {[a]=-1 \quad \therefore a \in[-1,0) \text { Reject }} \\ & \text { Case-2 }: \mathrm{a} \lt \frac{1}{2} \\ & -2 \mathrm{a}+1=[\mathrm{a}]+2 \mathrm{a} \\ & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{f} \\ & -2(\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{f})+1=\mathrm{I}+2 \mathrm{I}+2 \mathrm{f} \\ & \mathrm{I}=0, \mathrm{f}=\frac{1}{4} \quad \therefore \mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{4} \\ & \text { Hence } \mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{4} \\ & 72 \sum_{\mathrm{a} \in \mathrm{S}} \mathrm{a}=72 \times \frac{1}{4}=18\end{aligned}$
